reviews.comment: This prof be straight jestermaxxing
You're going to have to put extra effort into self-studying if you take this professor. I stopped showing up to class entirely once I realized he was only asking iClicker questions once a month.

Although the professor did put effort into his lectures, his teaching style was overall not very effective. He had a tendency of jumping straight into practice problems without properly explaining the underlying conceptual information. Additionally, his lecture notes were entirely handwritten, which made it more difficult to properly follow along.

Lectures felt disorganized and all over the place, and he wasn't great at explaining new concepts. He was a chill guy though and made some great jokes. I'd say to take this professor if you want a nice guy and are fine learning everything on your own.

Ricardo Eusebi is a physics dad over at Texas A&M, known for big brain energy but sigma grindset lectures. Students say he drops mad rizz during office hours, but his lives be giga hard to make sense of. His vibes are demanding and need steady grind and practice.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ricardo Eusbei is a solid physics professor at Texas A&M. His lectures are clear and organized, and he explains difficult concepts in a way that's easier to understand. He's approachable and willing to help if you have questions. Overall, a good class experience.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Ricardo Eusbei is an outstanding physics professor at Texas A&M. He explains complex ideas with clarity and passion, making every lecture engaging and meaningful. He genuinely cares about his students and goes above and beyond to help them succeed. Highly recommend!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: should've majored in business

The professor has a great sense of humor, I'll give him that. That being said, I feel that his teaching style wasn't very conducive to our learning. I ended up doing a lot of self-studying for this class as a result.
This professor did not prepare us for our exams at all. Lectures were long-winded and had nothing to do with the exam material.
This professor teaches content that is completely different from the exams, and I overall feel like I wasn't properly prepared for them.

I had a torn ACL and had surgery missing 5 weeks of classes with documented absences. I was 0.4 points away from getting the next letter grade, if I had credit for an absence on iclicker I would've gotten it. I notified this guy and he didn't give me the points pointing out the syllabus policy being clear. No humanity.

I would 100% recommend taking this class at a community college for anyone that has the chance to. This professor's lectures for this class failed to properly prepare us for the immense difficulty of the exams. This professor also has handwritten notes that are hard to read, so I ended up using another professor's notes to study for this class.

As a whole, the professor failed to properly teach us the content related to this course. Additionally, the professor would only ask iClicker questions once a month, so if you missed class on one of those days, your grade would take a big hit. Also, out of all the PHYS 207 professors, this one has the most confusing lecture slides.

I personally wouldn't recommend this professor. Overall, his explanations in class were long-winded and vague. He also did not do a great job of preparing us for the exams. The example problems he would complete in class were nothing like the exams. Lots of self-studying was necessary when I took this class.

Ricardo is a nice guy overall and brings humor to his lectures. Make sure that you are solid with note-taking reason; his note-taking process can be all over the place, and often reading the textbook (which is a super convoluted Pearson text) can be helpful. Homework sucks. It's long, tedious, and harder than the exams; I never got the point.

He definitely knows the subject and wants to help, has a laid back approach towards teaching which can make it hard to stay engaged. DO YOUR HOMEWORK AND EXTRA PRACTICE!! Exams are actually doable if you but in the time.

Not a great professor, to say the least. Out of every prof for this class, his notes were by far the worst. Showing up to lecture was essentially pointless because he was the absolute worst at explaining things. 0/10 experience, do not recommend to anyone.
Can't believe this dude made me miss my grandma's funeral to watch a block slide down a ramp
Eusebi the type of guy to add his name to your lab report just to increase his h-index

Overall, this professor is not great at explaining concepts. He has purely handwritten notes that are hard to follow along with. He also only rarely asks iClicker questions in class, so if you miss class on one of those days, your grade takes a big hit. I would recommend avoiding this class altogether and instead taking it at a community college.

PHYS 206 is a nightmare of a course (definitely a weed-out class). Make sure you're present in class for  Dr. Eusebi's iClickers -- he doesn't do many of them, so it's important to get the ones that he has available right. He covers the conceptual component of the course very well but tends to rush in his lectures and isn't great for homework help.

206 is an incredibly hard class, especially if you've never taken phys before. That being said, Eusebi is one of the better profs for this course. His teaching style helped me to do well on the conceptual questions. However, you will have to teach yourself a lot, but that's typical for any prof for 206. His demonstrations were helpful. Take him!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Eusebi is very knowledgeable, however I did not take to his teaching style. Dr. Eusebi's handwriting was hard to read and other profs, Dr. May, had good slides. I did awful on the 1st and 2nd exams, but bought A+ tutoring and it saved my grade. Get A+ before the first exam if you struggle and you will probably get an A. Take practice exams!!!

Eusebi's lectures are great content wise, but only really help conceptually for the exams given. You are expected to learn most of the work from your textbook and homework which is typically expected from any engineering course. Attendance is mandatory if you want the IClicker points. Only downside is that his handwriting is hard to read.

PHYS 206 is weed out class and difficult if you're not putting in the work. Dr. Eusebi, however, is extremely willing to help you understand the topics and is the reason why I was able to secure an A. He does demonstrations in class to help visualize and gives great example problems to study. HIGHLY recommend going to office hours prepared.

He was fine. The class is set up as to where it doesn't matter who your professor is. I didn't go to class, but his slides were very helpful. He wasn't very helpful outside of class, and IClicker was based on whether you got the question correct.

If you're determined to take the class instead of taking it over the summer: DONT. Learn from me, it is so much easier to do it during the summer online before third semester at wtc college or lone star. Unless you need to actually know this subject for a large portion of your major, this class is strictly made to weed you out. Period.

Go to class and use the previous exams to study. The homework took a lot of time, so be smart and pace them out rather than cramming them in the few days before they are due. The material in this class is somewhat difficult to grasp, but Dr. Eusebi does a good job of communicating the topics and math behind them.
He is cool
he is COOL!!!
he is good

PHYS 207 during Fall Semester. Prof Eusebi provides very detailed notes that he presents during lecture. There is a weekly recitation class scheduled that is TA driven. This course is University Physics so there are common exams. Be careful with your IClicker submissions. The homework can be challenging. Notes provided are valuable for exam prep!

Dr. Eusebi has an infectious passion for what he teaches, and he works hard to make the class interesting even if physics isn't everyone's favorite subject. I really enjoyed taking 206 with him. I was struggling a little on the homework the first half of the semester, but after that things started to click.

Has a really heavy accent and speeds through a lot of content. His handwriting is very messy to the point where I gave up trying to understand and fell asleep for most of the lectures. The common exams are really hard because the practices are not useful at all; you are completely blindsided by the content. PHYS 206 is just a really hard class :(
GOAT. My work was sub-par for my honors assignment. He gave me a 70 because he is a GOAT.

PHYS 207 is a very hard class but Eusebi is a solid professor to take. He's a clear lecturer who in my opinion has a good balance between explaining theory and working out problems and giving examples.

Eusubi is an extremely solid choice for 207; However, the clicker questions he does in class are inconsistent and extremely annoying. Exams are very fair, and there are plenty of chances for easy grades. Homework can be somewhat difficult.

Dr. Eusebi is a standard professor for 207, he has too many students to really make any personal connections in class. This is class is at times hard to visualize and you either understand the material well or not. I have had to pay for outside tutoring services to try to do better on the exams because the average on the exams are normally low
Eusebi is a solid professor. University Physics was not that bad, especially if you have taken physics in highschool. His lectures are very useful. Sometimes he has clicker quizzes.

I really liked Eusebi. One of the best 206/207 profs in my opinion. It's certainly a hard class, but he is a great teacher, and actually quite a nice guy (despite first impressions). He posts all the lecture notes. The problems he works out in class are very similar to tests.

Lectures are so unorganized and you can barely read what he writes sometimes. Nice guy, but you'll be doing most of the learning by yourself. Lot's of clicker quizzes but they're random so you won't have one every single class.

Physics is hard in general, but Eusebi lectures well. He has an accent but it's not terrible and his handwriting is hard to read but you can ask him and he'll tell you what he wrote. He's nice and helpful, the tests are just difficult (but it's physics). Make sure to have a high grade on online hw bc it'll help. also clicker questions !!! Take him!
Very knowledgeable and good at explaining things. Always makes himself available to you when possible. Willing to help. Handwriting is tough to read but lectures are easy to follow and understand.

Definitely the best prof I've had so far. The lectures are fantastic and easy to engage with, and his (Spanish?) accent is charming. I'm terrible about attendance, so sometimes I have to read more to get the topic, but if you go to lecture you'll probably understand it well. He walks you through each topic thoroughly.

I didn't find his class too painful. Combined with recitation, the class is very doable. He's a reasonable guy, and his accent isn't strong enough to be distracting. He generally prepared us well for common exams.

This class was the hardest one I had to take thus far. Tests are worth 80% of the grade and don't be discouraged if the first test grade is about a 50%. It gets better as the semester progresses. You have to put in a lot of work for this class. The best advise I can give is to study the practice exams for each exam AND THE FINAL.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Eusebi is by far the best 207 prof. He is a really nice guy and really easy to talk to. Office hours are the sole reason I passed this class because he was really helpful in them. However, if you have the chance to take don't panic or take this class at Blinn, take it.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No matter who you have, this course is difficult, but Dr. Eusebi is really helpful if you go see him in office hours. He really cares about his students and wants all of them to succeed. So, if you need help, just ask. Sometimes, he comes across a little terse, but he's not trying to be mean.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Highly recommend reading the university physics book to get an A. There's a good amount of homework, but it helps with the tests. The lectures aren't amazing and sometimes have clicker questions, but are sometimes funny/interesting. Eusebi is very understanding
He was an great professor with amazing lectures and is by far the best University Physics professor!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Eusebi's class. Speaking to others about their 218 professors, Eusebi works more example problems than most and explain things better. He has a bit of an accent, but after a couple lectures it wasn't much of a problem for me. In my opinion Eusebi is one of the better 218 profs, and he seems to care what students think. Would recommend.

Took his for physics 218 as a freshman. Usually accents are easy for me, but his was thick and made comprehending the already difficult material even harder. Terrible handwriting also impacted my note taking. Dislike random clicker quizzes, but other teacher's do that too.

His tests were pretty much about the same questions from the homework. Physics 208 is not an easy class, with that being said, don't expect an easy A. He is caring and will make sure you understand the material. It will help you a lot if you go to office hours as well when you don't understand.
Eusebi is one of the better 218 professors, it seems he really cares about students. Going to his office hours are very helpful.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The course in general is hard. He has an accent that makes him a little difficult to understand. Use the textbook for extra practice in the problems.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very good professor; Lectures weren't bad, and accent is very nice to listen to. Only real complaint is that he only seems to offer classes in the late evenings.

Decent lectures, but does provide tons of examples of each topic. Course is fast paced and if you're not already good at physics, you will need to spend problem after problem on your own time. Tests are now common exams and lecture does not prepare you for them. Do tons of problems. Fortunately, there's a new grading system to student's advantage.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a great teacher, knows his stuff, wants you to succeed. With the new Physics 218 redesign, every test is a common exam, and I think he prepares you the best for all the tests. Physics 218 is going to be hard despite what professor you choose, if you stay on top of all the work, then you'll do fine in the course.

He is a very good/smart professor. I just don't think he really understands what the exams are over (which are commons exams btw). He goes over difficult problems. He really cares about people's grades, gives a good distribution of the grades too. He had 2 exam reviews towards the end of the course. FEW clicker quizzes, which everyone did in groups
If you work to understand the formulas he gives and go to his office hours, you will be fine.

Eusebi is one of the best physics professors that teach at Texas A&M. Attending office hours is highly beneficial to your success in the class, especially if you go in with good questions. Trying to learn physics without doing a ton of problems for practice is unrealistic, regardless of the prof you have. Btw, he restates anything you can't read.

If he received a grade in penmanship or clarity it would reflect the average on the PHYS218  exam 3. The course is difficult due to the material and he knows a lot but he is not the best at translating it to his students. The only way to do well in the class is to complete countless problems from the book till you hopefully understand the material.
Worst teacher ever. Cannot write at all and assumes that you know how to get to the final answer and doesn't explain any of his problems. Do not take him at all by far the worst teacher ever

Eusebi is a good instructor who teaches the material very well. He has a lot of knowledge and is aware that the course is hard in general. You have to work hard in this course to earn a good grade regardless of the professor. But only take Eusebi if Dhar isn't available.

He is a very enthusiastic teacher. I enjoyed going to his lectures. Physics 218 is hard but he made it better. The curve wasn't that great. There are clicker quizzes in his class. Be ready to work hard.

People are saying his tests are harder than other professor's, but the exams are common exams, so every professor has the same ones.  I thought he was a great professor, physics is just a hard class.  Trust me, if you have to take 218, he's the one to take it from.

He is a fairly decent instructor at the lectures. He knows it's a difficult course by nature, and he is willing to help you. Although he has an accent, he is aware of it and tries to ensure that the class can understand the material despite it. I would definitely recommend.

Eusebi is a great prof, dont get me wrong this class is hard as nuts but he is extremely helpful and his accent is not to bad. You will get alot out of his class. Word to the wise don't answer any question unless you are sure you know the answer

Eusebi wasn't bad of a teacher at all! I always asked questions after class when I needed a better understanding and he helped a lot. I really recommend attending every class; physics is just plain hard in general! His grades are based on a point-scale. Good Luck!

He's a great person, but very bad instructor. He thinks we know everything he does. His tests are insanely hard, harder than other profs, but that's also the nature of the course in general. If you are active in class, go to recitation, and use his office hours you should do fine.
Awesome teacher. Hard class
